entities.name: Fatimid architecture
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary: The Fatimid architecture that developed in the Fatimid Caliphate (909–1171 CE) of North Africa combined elements of eastern and western architecture, drawing on Abbasid architecture, Byzantine, Ancient Egyptian, Coptic architecture and North African traditions; it bridged early Islamic styles and the medieval architecture of the Mamluks of Egypt, introducing many innovations.
